| | Growing up, it wasn't cool to teach people to hate themselves and others based on skin pigmentation.

Yet, that's exactly what's being pushed hard in public universities nationwide, even in "conservative" Idaho.

As Elon Musk recently stated, [**DEI must die.**](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=c046b38eb5&e=dea908e0fe "see his post")

The guy running against me, the same one I beat last time, has repeatedly voted to fully fund it.

In contrast... **_I'm working to abolish it._**

This is because abolishing DEI offices aligns with the goal of Idaho law: to secure freedom from discrimination for everyone in the state and to eliminate preferential treatment based on race, sex, or other factors.

Under DEI offices, our universities have hosted black-only or LGBT-only graduation events!

For instance, Boise State’s Student Equity Center, which claims to promote diversity and advocate for equity, hosts several racially discriminatory ceremonies, like the “Black Excellence Stole Celebration” for black students, LGBTQ-only graduation ceremonies, and the “LatinX Stole Celebration” for Latinx students.

The University of Idaho recently started the Black Cultural Center to provide a “safe space for black students.” The center's director, Mario Pile, aims to recruit more black students to enroll at the university.

_**This violates Idaho law.**_

That's why I'm advocating for [the elimination of offices](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=db93c590d9&e=dea908e0fe "why kill DEI?") that support such activities.

Utah just passed [a bill ](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=b6e1d34259&e=dea908e0fe "what'd Utah do?")in the state house to do this. Oklahoma, Florida, and Texas have already done it too.

So, _why not Idaho?_

Cheers,

Brian

**P.S.**

The Daily Caller recently featured me in an article about getting rid of DEI. [Click here to read it](https://votelenney.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ce84224f3cc6e52f7633cc60&id=f17f19daf6&e=dea908e0fe "see it").

Friend,
---
Democrats in Wisconsin are going to great lengths to obstruct our election security efforts.
---
A left-wing judge with longtime ties to liberal Governor Tony Evers made a ruling earlier this month _**ALLOWING**_ ballot curing statewide for this year’s election.
---
Ballot curing is the process of “correcting” ballots containing incorrect information about the voter. The process allows election clerks to subjectively address ballot discrepancies such as missing signatures and wrong addresses.
---

Roger Williams is a Christian, conservative, pro-life, and second amendment supporter taking Texas values to Washington, D.C. He is a small business owner with over 45 years of experience and is running for Congress to create economic growth, jobs, and provide strong leadership. Roger worked alongside President Trump to fight against high taxes, rising energy prices, and soaring healthcare costs. His passion for conservative leadership led him to support Republican candidates from the White House to the county courthouse. Peter,

51 years ago, _Roe v. Wade_ became the law of the land when the Supreme Court ruled that women had the right to make their own reproductive healthcare decisions without interference from any state up until viability. Yet, thanks to an extremely conservative Supreme Court in the summer of 2022, decades of progress and precedent were overturned.

This set the stage for the return of draconian laws taking medical decision-making away from women and their doctors. We've already seen how devastating this decision has been. Immediately following the ruling, fourteen states worked to pass a near-total ban on abortion. Seven more chose to pass some of the most restrictive abortion access laws in the country.

Now Republicans are in control of the House, and political analysts suggest a Republican sweep in November is possible–meaning abortion is once again on the ballot. This time, not as a Supreme Court decision, but as the potential for a national ban on abortion that would supersede state laws that protect women. While we may not be able to celebrate _Roe_ Day as we used to, its importance is something we cannot forget.

As a doctor, I know that deeply personal reproductive health care decisions should be made by a patient in consultation with her doctor. Extremist politicians in D.C. must not make medical decisions.

That's why last year, I worked to reintroduce the Let Doctors Provide Reproductive Health Care Act to ensure every woman has access to the reproductive health care she needs.

It is also why, just last week, I voted against a bill that would take money away from programs for needy families and use it to support sham Crisis Pregnancy Centers. These centers masquerade as clinics, offering free pregnancy tests and ultrasounds, often without any healthcare provider. Then, they lie to patients and spew anti-abortion rhetoric meant to stop women from considering abortion. Make no mistake, this bill passed the Republican House and is part of their march toward a national abortion ban.

| Fifty-one years ago today, the Supreme Court voted in favor of _Roe v. Wade_ , the landmark case that enshrined reproductive rights as the law of the land. Despite decades of majority support for protecting the right to choose, the Supreme Court’s conservative majority voted to overturn more than 50 years of precedent. The conservative Court took away our national rights.

Since then, extreme Republicans have introduced legislation to criminalize abortion and ban contraception. Twenty-one states currently have extreme abortion bans – **and it’s only a matter of time before extremist Republicans try to impose a federal ban.**

Women across the country are experiencing heartbreaking, life-threatening circumstances as they’re denied the healthcare they need. No case has been as representative of the healthcare future women can expect under extreme Republican legislation than Kate Cox’s story. After being diagnosed with health-threatening pregnancy complications, Kate was denied an abortion in Texas and was forced to travel out of state.

This election cycle, Republicans are telling us they’ll take away that right too if given the chance–they’ll make a national abortion ban the law of the land. body:
| | Peter –

Since extreme Republicans led by Donald Trump overturned _Roe v. Wade_ two years ago, women in Texas have died from pregnancy-related complications, been forced to travel out of state for abortions, and faced lawsuits for helping their loved ones get access to abortion medication.

As a trauma surgeon, I know firsthand the life-threatening consequences of anti-choice legislation. Over the years — even before _Roe_ was overturned — I’ve operated on women facing death from reproductive emergencies.

We all have the right to choose when and how to start a family. As a father to my daughter, I want her to grow up in a world where she is happy, healthy, and has the right to make her own choices about her body.

That’s why this fight is important to me.

**We must stand against extremists interfering in the doctor-patient relationship.** One of the most dire threats our state faces is the denial of reproductive health rights held by Texas women for nearly 50 years.

On this anniversary of _Roe v. Wade_ , I will continue fighting to restore abortion rights, ensure Texans have access to the full range of birth control options, and protect private medical information.

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/77551252/450759560/2045957508?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQxNjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmY0NGM1NWMtNzNiOS1lZTExLWJlYTEtMDAyMjQ4MjIzN2RhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=TeXmUPiMsOT_MLnz8Bybg25GUxbk76cef9j284_vWDM=&emci=ac305bf2-5fb9-ee11-bea1-0022482237da&emdi=6f44c55c-73b9-ee11-bea1-0022482237da&ceid=10481059)

| | Peter — Over fifty years ago, the Supreme Court issued the landmark decision _Roe v. Wade_ which guaranteed the right to privacy and reproductive freedom for women all over the country, but two years ago, that decision was overturned. In the last year, several states have banned or severely limited abortion rights, with others working toward _even more_ bans and restrictions. Despite the majority of Americans supporting the right to choose when or whether to have a family, the out-of-touch politicians in Washington have prioritized their petty arguments and partisan soundbites over protecting basic reproductive freedoms. **So, it's time to send a forceful voice for change to Congress to fight for reproductive health care and protect our communities. In the last year, several states have banned or severely limited abortion rights, with others working toward even more bans and restrictions. body:
The Swamp agrees to throw America under the bus.
| | [ ](http://links.gopmembership.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=3ae8e746d9f8422fb3ae0a20aab1ef16&_e=T2FEwOcX4Pud-C5-tMko8bBaB-nLSXXD5Z-wn-GHSebLxjf7t7BA01EaA1nC4OscrCfZjWSW8eCD-4z4UArBRVdxJDQKIGssCJwC6scURdZXPpQM5CTZwgxVaRYPzZIhQrz2_w9vleZLGExmublU1B3h0VY-4ANoN_lmuVack0H41a-GPVnkFJZU9pZ6tloe1fMJcGL4DWCSxjuplEdWd5PFDmMpfuiRJY6FNRXu1sFUxkwDHSRfZSAs-9J70evmuiHAMxI-uNkdiX8fWcD7CRqgW6r1HQ5x14X6CYrn96U%3D)

Fellow American, Right now, America is being invaded. But the only thing Washington can agree on is selling out America by increasing spending, inflating our national debt, and providing NO real solution. _**The crisis at our southern border is NOT something that we can just ignore.**_ Americans are being put in danger thanks to the Uniparty's inability to take action. We have illegal immigrants flooding across the border EVERY DAY, and we have no idea who is coming into our country. And the best Congress can come up with is slapping a band-aid on this crisis with continuing resolutions. If you have an overflowing fire hydrant, you won't solve the problem by getting more buckets. You have to cut off the flow. _**So let me make one thing clear:**_ _**We need to close the border or close the government.**_ This is the leverage that we have and it's something the Republican Majority in the House needs to take advantage of instead of making destructive deals with Democrats. This isn't a time for Republicans to play nice. It's time to put the American people FIRST. Republicans must demand that the border be closed. That's why I am rallying patriots everywhere to help me lay the pressure on. _I need you to add your name to our letter of support so I can show House Republicans that Americans are sick and tired of them selling us out with continued resolutions.**You can h**_ _****elp d** emand a REAL solution to Biden's Border Crisis.**_ [**Join me today and tell Congress to Secure Our Border :**](http://links.gopmembership.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=3ae8e746d9f8422fb3ae0a20aab1ef16&_e=T2FEwOcX4Pud-C5-tMko8bBaB-nLSXXD5Z-wn-GHSebLxjf7t7BA01EaA1nC4OscrCfZjWSW8eCD-4z4UArBRVdxJDQKIGssCJwC6scURdZXPpQM5CTZwgxVaRYPzZIhQrz2_w9vleZLGExmublU1Cd3aMdia1H5NpPqrGWbrBD7u5ilaA1BXsWKwGcaq4SZbKsJZnN2JRgiu9XIWl0k3s9J9FM4DI95ZP9kN8rbdLjnUuk_ZneX5d1LZeFuORyoOsHLwPWl0vuQFM7plpShZPgT6MxiLxR1JWGCKz5x1u4%3D)
| [ **SECURE OUR BORDER** ](http://links.gopmembership.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=3ae8e746d9f8422fb3ae0a20aab1ef16&_e=T2FEwOcX4Pud-C5-tMko8bBaB-nLSXXD5Z-wn-GHSebLxjf7t7BA01EaA1nC4OscrCfZjWSW8eCD-4z4UArBRVdxJDQKIGssCJwC6scURdZXPpQM5CTZwgxVaRYPzZIhQrz2_w9vleZLGExmublU1NbvMej8LeNZHvLYb3M5zmCZK_QSxGbO_ZHI8Fd0FB_ovgir8t6Pe5PTPeuLP_th8fTv5ddyFj9nvkdN5Q5UVBSx-J9Cu4cgkAO8Cw98zIIPVoRbW1aLHWJAO4b4v-ap8lilrnZdGAnQQKI60ON7xzg%3D)

It's hard enough to stop the far-left's state-sponsored invasion of our southern border, and it's even harder when Republicans are bending the knee to their radical agenda. But unlike so many in Congress, I came to Washington to Save America, I did not come to make my pockets fatter. Truthfully, that hasn't made me many friends. **In fact, it 's made me a major threat to the establishment's status quo of selling our nation to the highest bidder.** Fellow American, I rely on the generosity of folks like you to support my fight to Drain the Swamp because I refuse to take a single dollar from the DC lobbyists and PACs. [**So, after you add your name, I hope you will stand with me by chipping in to my campaign.**](http://links.gopmembership.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=3ae8e746d9f8422fb3ae0a20aab1ef16&_e=T2FEwOcX4Pud-C5-tMko8bBaB-nLSXXD5Z-wn-GHSebLxjf7t7BA01EaA1nC4OscrCfZjWSW8eCD-4z4UArBRVdxJDQKIGssCJwC6scURdZXPpQM5CTZwgxVaRYPzZIhQrz2_w9vleZLGExmublU1L4KAn0j41ty127mMfl8QWDB-SgfvXBfXmcorUdWh04ldLYsSPHq_IYRF60R5os5F98ML68vJ3yaQnsMZkzqNc9AvNrnF5MAuLC3yOreOMCUT8PQaWy-lf1ofi3aMeFGPgJtbtAIRWktXdaQos-XwLM%3D) With your support, I can continue to fight to put an end to Biden's Border Crisis and do what needs to be done to put America First. _Thanks for standing strong,_ Matt Gaetz

_We know how the rest of the story goes._

After Donald Trump won the White House and forced three anti-choice justices onto the Supreme Court, Roe was overturned — paving the way for the extreme abortion bans we’re seeing today all across the country.

It’s a horrifying reality for millions of Americans. **_But these extreme Republicans aren’t done yet._**

Jacky Rosen is exactly who we want in the Senate to keep fighting for reproductive freedom. Right now, CNN analysts are calling Jacky one of the most vulnerable senators in the race that will likely decide Senate control, and a shady billionaire has already poured $2 million into Nevada to flip her seat for Republicans. Jacky's strong stance on reproductive rights is one of the reasons why the GOP has made her a top target for defeat – and that’s exactly why we need to do everything we possibly can to help her win in Nevada and defend our Democratic Senate majority this year. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Tina Smith and Jacky Rosen will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = We’re in the fight of our lives when it comes to reproductive rights. Thank you for being part of this important work. Wade_ was in place, we had more work to do to guarantee _access_ to abortion care. But in 2022, the Supreme Court revoked this right, removing federal protection and paving the way for many states that have since enacted extreme abortion bans. Soon after the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , Michigan voters passed a ballot measure that enshrined the right to abortion and all reproductive care into our state’s Constitution. Now, Michigan is a haven in the Midwest.
This victory would not have been possible without the reproductive justice activists on the ground doing the work to protect our fundamental human rights. **With people power, we refused to allow the far-right Supreme Court to take away our right to bodily autonomy.**
Reproductive Freedom for All Foundation is carrying on that momentum in Michigan and across the country, because millions of people in the U.S. can’t access the reproductive care they need. We won’t let this fundamental right get taken away. Instead, we must expand protections.

Hi Peter, it’s Raquel.
Today is the 51st anniversary of the landmark Roe v. Wade ruling that established constitutional protections for abortion.
In 2022, we saw our Supreme Court, led by far-right conservative judges, ignore decades of precedent and overturn Roe, stripping away our reproductive rights.
One of my most powerful lessons as a legislator was a state trip to El Salvador, where a total abortion ban is in place. Our delegation met with women sent to prison simply for having miscarriages or obstetric emergencies. I knew we could never let this happen here.
Right now, we’re seeing a state-by-state attack to reverse reproductive rights. Right here in Arizona, we are awaiting our conservative court’s ruling that considers enforcing abortion laws from the 18th century!
If Republicans are not stopped, we could be seeing an attempt to ban abortion nationally.
Despite our setbacks, I remain hopeful. Just yesterday, I joined thousands of people gathered at the Arizona Women’s March: people were signing petitions, training to be volunteers, and fighting back against extremist abortion restrictions.
‘Looking ahead’ after the August primary for our team will look like this: we will not slow down the campaign after winning. We'll be working tirelessly to pass Arizona’s ballot measure [https://arizonaforabortionaccess.org/] to protect the right to abortion.
Then, once Democrats retake the majority, Congress must act. That’s why I fully support codifying Roe into federal law. I know together, we can get it done.

subject: Reproductive freedom is a fundamental right. Period.

body:
On the anniversary of the landmark Roe v. Wade Supreme Court case, I can’t help but think of how much farther we have to go.
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/130?refcode=em20240122&t=1&akid=873%2E62735%2EzgmP1U)
Peter,
**Today marks the 51st anniversary of the landmark**** _Roe v. Wade_****Supreme Court ruling, which was decided on this day in 1973.**
_Roe_ enshrined the right to choose for Americans for decades — until the Court overruled its decision in 2022 and vindicated far-right Republicans’ attacks on reproductive freedom. I was furious when this decision came out.
But on this anniversary of _Roe v. Wade_ , I want to share what gives me hope.
Michigan is leading the charge to protect and expand reproductive rights. Last November, Governor Whitmer signed the Reproductive Health Act into law — strengthening abortion access for all, and breaking down barriers that disproportionately impact people of color and people struggling to make ends meet.
What’s more, we’ve seen other states do the same since the fall of _Roe_ , from Ohio to Maryland to Colorado.
Lastly, the fight on the federal level is far from over. Americans deserve a universal healthcare plan that ensures access to comprehensive reproductive healthcare, including contraception, family planning services, and safe, legal abortion — and I’m ready to take that fight straight to Washington.

clean_body: On the anniversary of the landmark Roe v. Wade Supreme Court case, I can’t help but think of how much farther we have to go. Peter, Today marks the 51st anniversary of the landmark Roe v. WadeSupreme Court ruling, which was decided on this day in 1973. Roe enshrined the right to choose for Americans for decades — until the Court overruled its decision in 2022 and vindicated far-right Republicans’ attacks on reproductive freedom. I was furious when this decision came out. But on this anniversary of Roe v. Wade , I want to share what gives me hope. Michigan is leading the charge to protect and expand reproductive rights. Last November, Governor Whitmer signed the Reproductive Health Act into law — strengthening abortion access for all, and breaking down barriers that disproportionately impact people of color and people struggling to make ends meet. What’s more, we’ve seen other states do the same since the fall of Roe , from Ohio to Maryland to Colorado. Lastly, the fight on the federal level is far from over. Americans deserve a universal healthcare plan that ensures access to comprehensive reproductive healthcare, including contraception, family planning services, and safe, legal abortion — and I’m ready to take that fight straight to Washington. We must protect reproductive rights. I’m not going to stand for Republicans dismantling our rights and freedoms — and that’s exactly what they’re trying to do. Tom is the proud husband to Rhonda and the proud father to two beautiful daughters. Their family resides in the wonderful city of Westfield, New Jersey. Tom's commitment to the people of New Jersey has been inspired by a legacy of **dedicated public service** from his grandfather, former U.S. Representative Robert Kean, to his father, former Governor Thomas H. Kean Sr. Kean has always understood and recognized the importance of civic engagement and is honored to **represent the people of New Jersey's 7th Congressional District** in Congress. From his early days in the Environmental Protection Agency during the George H.W. Bush Administration (where he met his incredible wife Rhonda), to serving as a volunteer firefighter and an emergency medical technician in Washington, D.C. — Tom has always had a heart for making our world a better, freer, safer place. Determined to answer the call to public service again, Tom Kean Jr. believed he, personally, could turn ideas into action and make a lasting difference in people’s lives. In 2001, Tom was elected to the New Jersey General Assembly, and two years later, was named to the upper house of the state legislature after his tireless work in ethics reform. Then in 2008, his peers unanimously elected him Republican Leader in the New Jersey Senate. Shortly thereafter, he unveiled his caucus’ job creation package, **“Common-Sense Plan for a More Affordable New Jersey,”** which ultimately reversed the course that previous administrations were quickly leading the state down. To this day, Tom continues to build upon his proven track record of delivering for the people of New Jersey in Congress:
* **Passed legislation advocating for Veteran-Owned small businesses**
* **Passed legislation to improve commuter rail transportation**
* **Passed a resolution affirming strong US support for Ukraine**
* **Passed legislation to support mental health for school children**

Today is the anniversary of Roe v. Wade
Peter,
**Today is the 51st anniversary of Roe v. Wade, the historic Supreme Court case that guaranteed the federal right to abortion care.**
But instead of celebrating this anniversary today, we’re witnessing an all-out assault on abortion rights and reproductive care in states across the country—including in Texas.
Since Roe was overturned, 21 states have passed extreme bans on abortion, leaving close to 30 million women without life-saving reproductive care. And in states like Texas where there are little to no exceptions to the ban, patients are being forced to carry nonviable and dangerous pregnancies to term.
In 2024 we have the opportunity to fight back against this assault on our freedoms. We can defeat Trump, unseat extreme anti-choice Republicans, and codify abortion rights with a Democratic Congress and White House. But we can only do it together.

name: =?utf-8?Q?State=20Representative=20Ryan=20Chamberlin?=
subject: Weekly Update from Rep. Ryan Chamberlin
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/official-newsletter-12675428?e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| |
---
| | **WEEKLY UPDATE FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN**
---
| My fellow Floridians,

We had another productive week in Tallahassee! Last week, it was great to meet with constituents, stakeholders, and fellow elected officials to discuss how we can build a better future for Florida. As State Representative, I promise to put the good people of District 24 first, and I am committed to ensuring that your voice is heard. I truly appreciate your continued trust and support!

Thank you for reading this recap of some of the great things that happened in Tallahassee. I look forward to keeping you updated on my work in the Florida House.
---
|
---
| | **Tuesday, January 16**
---
|
---
| I had the pleasure of meeting with students and faculty from Belleview High School during Agriculture Day at the Capitol. It was wonderful to talk with these bright students from District 24 and learn more about the issues important to them.
---
|
---
| It was great to meet with representatives from the Marion County Farm Bureau to discuss their legislative priorities and ongoing projects within our county. I look forward to working with them during this year’s legislative session to support our farmers and ranchers in District 24.
---
|
---
| I had the honor of discussing legislative priorities with John Frazier, a constituent from Marion County and member of the Florida Chiropractic Association. We talked about his work in the district and the association’s legislative priorities.
---
|
---
| It was a privilege to meet with the YMCA of Central Florida and their CEO Kevin Bolding. We had an in-depth conversation about the ongoing and potential appropriations projects needed in Marion and Brevard counties. This wonderful organization has helped many Central Florida families succeed, so it is an honor to fight for their needs in the Florida House.
---
| | **Wednesday, January 17**
---
|
---
| It was great to have a visit from Isis LaRose from Better Together to discuss how I can assist the organization and its projects in Marion County and around the state. Better Together works hard to help Floridians thrive by keeping families together and preventing child abuse and neglect before it happens.
---
|
---
| I had the pleasure of meeting with Marion County Clerk Greg Harrell during Clerk’s Association Day at the Capitol. We had the opportunity to discuss important projects in our county and legislative priorities. It is always an honor to welcome fellow Marion County residents and public servants to my office in Tallahassee.
---
|
---
| It was wonderful to visit with Legislative Manager Matt Cretul and members of the Marion County Commission. We enjoyed a lengthy discussion regarding important legislation and appropriations projects. I am always so encouraged by those who want to be involved in the legislative process and are willing to make the trip to Tallahassee.
---
|
---
| I had the pleasure of attending a reception for the Florida Senior Living Association after a full day of session. It was great to meet with the members and discuss [HB 995](https://voteryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=385fc83d62&e=d1c1b9864f), a bill that would directly impact assisted living facilities in Florida. I greatly appreciated their input!
---
|
---
---
| My fellow legislators and I had a great time on the field for the Florida legislature’s 41st annual King of the Hill Softball Game. Republicans faced off against Democrats in a fun-filled night. I am proud to announce that the Republican team took home the win!
---
| | **Thursday, January 18**
---
|
---
| It was great to meet with some members of the Marion County School Board to discuss legislative priorities and ongoing projects in the district. Education is an important issue to me, and I look forward to working alongside the board to improve our public school system.
---
| | **Week 2: Committee Meetings**
---
| We made a lot of progress during committee meetings last week. It is an honor to play such a significant role in the future of our state, and I look forward to seeing many of our bills succeed on the House floor in the upcoming weeks.

I met with the following committees during the week:
* Select Committee on Health Innovation
* Regulatory Reform and Economic Development Subcommittee
* Judiciary Committee - Additional progress has been made on [HB 1](https://voteryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=61efeab5c4&e=d1c1b9864f)! It passed favorably in its last committee stop.
* Civil Justice Subcommittee
* Education Equality Subcommittee - We had the opportunity to hear [HB 545](https://voteryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=153a128257&e=d1c1b9864f) by Rep. Berny Jacques. This legislation would prevent adult students convicted of felonies from competing in high school sports.

---
|
---
| | I am working hard for you and your family in Tallahassee! Thank you for electing me to serve you. It is the highest honor to represent you in the Florida Legislature.

I look forward to keeping you updated on my work during the 2024 Legislative Session. As always, if I may be of any assistance, please do not hesitate to contact my office by **[clicking here](https://voteryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=aad263854b&e=d1c1b9864f "https://www.myfloridahouse.gov/Sections/Representatives/contactmember.aspx?MemberId=4901&SessionId=103&utm_source=Ryan+Chamberlin+for+State+Representative&utm_campaign=ae0a433299-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_12_08_05_14_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-7ddd94a0de-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D")**.

Best regards,

**Ryan Chamberlin**
******State Representative**
**District 24**
---
| |
---
| _Copyright © 2024 State Representative Ryan Chamberlin, All rights reserved._
State Representative Ryan Chamberlin

**Our mailing address is:**
1101 The Capitol
402 South Monroe Street
Tallahassee, FL 32399-1300

Want to change how you receive these emails?
You can [update your preferences](https://voteryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/profile?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=929c76fdea&e=d1c1b9864f&c=c991a04a9e) or [unsubscribe from this list](https://voteryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/unsubscribe?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=929c76fdea&e=d1c1b9864f&c=c991a04a9e).

That's why I am proudly endorsing my friend Republican Max Ukropina for Congress in Orange County's 47th District ... and I'm writing to urge you to do the same.

I hope you'll join me in supporting Max today and contributing whatever you can to help send him to Washington and let him know you have his back. | Peter,

Today would have marked the 51st anniversary of _Roe v. Wade_. After generations of women led mobilization efforts across the country, _Roe v. Wade_ enshrined reproductive freedom as a constitutional right. For decades after, this landmark Supreme Court decision decriminalized abortion, expanded access to abortion services, and significantly improved the lives and health of women and families.

In 2022, a Supreme Court with a conservative majority overturned 50 years of precedent despite decades of national consensus. Since then, 21 states have enacted extreme abortion bans, criminalizing women seeking abortions and their doctors and even going after contraception.

Peter, Republicans aren’t stopping there; they’ve already threatened to impose a federal ban on abortion. Millions more stand to lose their fundamental freedom to reproductive healthcare access under Republican control.

Today, on what would have been _Roe v. Wade’s_ 51st anniversary, I reaffirm my commitment to reproductive justice. That includes combating extremist legislation that further infringes on that right and passing legislation that expands and safeguards reproductive rights.

| | Today should have marked 51 years since the right to choose was enshrined by the Supreme Court under _Roe v. Wade_. Instead, it's a reminder of the freedom that millions of Americans lost 19 months ago when _Roe_ was overturned — and it's a moment to recommit to restoring those rights. Since the _Dobbs_ decision, headline after headline has exposed the reality of the far-right's war on reproductive freedom and the constitutional right to privacy:
* Women denied the reproductive health care they need in emergency rooms
* Doctors refusing to provide care for fear of retribution
* Women forced to flee their home states in order to seek basic care in a state that will provide it
* People facing criminal investigations for miscarriages

The list of horrors goes on and on. And the forces behind _Dobbs_ don't want it to stop. **When it comes to the Republicans and their war on reproductive freedom, cruelty is the point.** The party that claims to be "pro-life" is the same party denying life-saving health care and forcing women to bring children into a country that denies families access to affordable child care, paid leave, and basic resources for working parents. But I refuse to give up hope in our democracy's ability to correct course. An overwhelming majority of Americans support protecting the right to reproductive freedom – and we've seen it manifest itself at the ballot box repeatedly in the wake of _Roe's_ repeal. States including Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Kansas, and Montana have either passed constitutional protections for reproductive health care or defeated proposed abortion bans. **This is not a red-state-against-blue-state issue; this is a fundamental question about the right to live your life free from government intrusion, and voters have been delivering a clear message.** I'm proud to be from a state that has some of the strongest abortion protections in the nation. But I am never taking those protections for granted, and I am fighting every day for the people in other states who have lost their reproductive rights or will soon see them ripped away by far-right lawmakers. I'm committed to electing a Congress in 2024 that will defend reproductive freedom at every level. That means expanding our slim Democratic majority in the Senate, and electing pro-choice Democrats here in Oregon and across the country to help flip back the House. We must keep making our voices heard. Together, we can beat back anti-choice cruelty. Together, we can make it so that January 22 is once again a day of celebration for the rights we have — not the rights we lost. clean_body: | | | | Today should have marked 51 years since the right to choose was enshrined by the Supreme Court under Roe v. Wade. Instead, it's a reminder of the freedom that millions of Americans lost 19 months ago when Roe was overturned — and it's a moment to recommit to restoring those rights. Since the Dobbs decision, headline after headline has exposed the reality of the far-right's war on reproductive freedom and the constitutional right to privacy: Women denied the reproductive health care they need in emergency rooms Doctors refusing to provide care for fear of retribution Women forced to flee their home states in order to seek basic care in a state that will provide it People facing criminal investigations for miscarriages The list of horrors goes on and on. And the forces behind Dobbs don't want it to stop. When it comes to the Republicans and their war on reproductive freedom, cruelty is the point. The party that claims to be "pro-life" is the same party denying life-saving health care and forcing women to bring children into a country that denies families access to affordable child care, paid leave, and basic resources for working parents. But I refuse to give up hope in our democracy's ability to correct course. An overwhelming majority of Americans support protecting the right to reproductive freedom – and we've seen it manifest itself at the ballot box repeatedly in the wake of Roe's repeal. States including Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Kansas, and Montana have either passed constitutional protections for reproductive health care or defeated proposed abortion bans. This is not a red-state-against-blue-state issue; this is a fundamental question about the right to live your life free from government intrusion, and voters have been delivering a clear message. I'm proud to be from a state that has some of the strongest abortion protections in the nation. But I am never taking those protections for granted, and I am fighting every day for the people in other states who have lost their reproductive rights or will soon see them ripped away by far-right lawmakers. I'm committed to electing a Congress in 2024 that will defend reproductive freedom at every level. That means expanding our slim Democratic majority in the Senate, and electing pro-choice Democrats here in Oregon and across the country to help flip back the House. We must keep making our voices heard. Together, we can beat back anti-choice cruelty. Together, we can make it so that January 22 is once again a day of celebration for the rights we have — not the rights we lost. | Peter,

Fifty-one years ago, the Supreme Court issued _Roe v. Wade_ , codifying a woman’s right to choose. _Roe v. Wade’s_ impact is undeniable; it decriminalized abortions nationwide, expanded safe access to abortion, and helped improve the lives and health of generations of women and families.

Despite decades of national consensus, in 2022, a Supreme Court conservative majority overturned over 50 years of precedent. This ruling has since opened the door for attacks against access to contraception, extreme abortion bans, and the criminalization of women and doctors.

| The Supreme Court's 6-3 decision to overturn decades of abortion rights by overturning _Roe v. Wade_ was an egregious misstep and shameful stain on our country's history.

Today, on the 51st anniversary of _Roe v. Wade,_ and 2 years after its overturning, the fight to protect abortion access is more crucial than ever.

**Because the extremist Court isn't going to stop here — reading Justice Clarence Thomas's opinion on the overturning made that perfectly clear.** I want you to read what he wrote for yourself: | "...in future cases, we should reconsider all of this Court's substantive due process precedents, including _**Griswold, Lawrence, and Obergfell..."**_

**"We have a duty to "correct the error"** established in those precedents..."

_\- Justice Clarence Thomas (Page 117)_
---
_"Griswold, Lawrence, and Obergfell."_

Peter, here's what each of those landmark cases decided:

— _Griswold v. Connecticut_ made contraception legally accessible.
— _Lawrence v. Texas_ legalized same-sex relationships.
— _Obergfell v. Hodges_ legalized same-sex marriage.

**These fundamental rights are all vulnerable, Peter.**

| DEVELOPING... last week, our movement successfully averted a government shutdown AND fought off a MAGA attempt to completely gut environmental enforcement in the process.

Big Oil lobbyists are _furious_ -- and are now focusing their efforts on destructive Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) exports including a MASSIVE project on the Gulf Coast of Louisiana, called CP2 LNG.

If approved, this dangerous project would destroy coastal wetlands and spew toxic pollution into the environment and communities -- a yearly climate impact equal to the annual emissions of 53 coal-fired power plants or 43 million cars.

For the sake of our health and climate future, we must stop this project now. We have a tiny window to move the Biden administration to reassess LNG exports including this project.

**This is a moment when we need every LCV member to step up. To keep our grassroots campaign going and defend our climate future, we must raise $35,000 by next week -- and right now, we're falling short.**

[The best thing you can do right now is to renew your LCV membership today. For a limited time, every contribution will be TRIPLE MATCHED. Even $5 can make a difference >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/EZ_)

The truth is -- LNG exports aren't the only urgent environmental fight we're up against right now. There are so many reasons to pitch in -- here are just a few:
1. **Because MAGA Republicans are pushing _even harder_ to slash clean energy investments, zero out funding for environmental justice, and mandate more dirty drilling leases.** LCV is organizing quickly to mobilize grassroots pressure on Congress to reject reckless anti-environment proposals. [But at the end of the day, the impact we can have will depend on our members.](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/EZ_)

[The environmental movement CANNOT sit this fight out. We need you, Peter.](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/EZ_)

[Peter, please don't sit this fight out. Renew your LCV membership for just $5 today while it will be triple matched >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/EZ_)

In June of 2022, I was honored to sponsor legislation that protected abortion rights right here in Delaware. House Bill 455 expanded abortion access and protected both providers and patients from anti-abortion laws in other states. **The very day after HB 455 passed the House, the Supreme Court released _Dobbs_ , all but overturning _Roe v. Wade_.** The content of the ruling was devastating, if not surprising. When Donald Trump was appointing three justices to the Court, he made it clear his top priority was to strip women of their reproductive freedoms. In Delaware, we kept moving forward. Four days after the _Dobbs_ decision, the Senate passed HB 455 and it was signed into law the very next day. **18 months later, on this anniversary of _Roe v. Wade_ , I'm reminded of the threat to all of us when the right to bodily autonomy is stripped from women.** Health decisions belong in the exam room, not in the halls of a legislative body or in a courtroom. We must elect a democratic trifecta this fall so we can do what the majority of Americans agree with — federally protect the right to abortion. **We protected the right to abortion in Delaware, but let's be clear: the moment Republicans are in control, they will ban abortion federally.** Thanks for hearing me out, Sarah | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/77555009/450771919/1954656641?refcode=EM_FL_MCB_20240122_na_roe_cand_nc_act_xx_img&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjI0OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZmJkYTE3MC04MWI5LWVlMTEtYmVhMS0wMDIyNDgyMjM3ZGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pqZj8TgTlav1tZdLKFiGza5S7sT6FL-x3pIurPf5LE4=)
